purpose: Finding 4 of docs/ARCHITECTURE_ATLAS_FEASIBILITY_REVIEW_2026_09_27.md (untracked review) for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: full-model quality under the deployment arithmetic contract, against the vendor reference, with the weights at the official checkpoint precision everywhere (FP8 E4M3 with UE8M0 32x32 block scales, FP4 E2M1 routed experts with UE8M0 per-32 scales, BF16/FP32 where the checkpoint stores them). The Qwen3-8B counterpart is results/quality/qwen3_8b_deployment_arithmetic.json; the acceptance rule is the same and was committed (d3eb0939) before any full-model result existed.
model: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, revision dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277 (HF cache, 476 GB): 40 backbone layers, hidden 5,120, 64 heads x 512 (MQA), 384 routed experts top-6 + 1 shared, hyper-connections x4 with 20 Sinkhorn iterations, compressed KV (ratio 2 on layers 2-19, 1 on 20-39) with the two-level indexer (top-512 of compressed positions; candidate blocks from layer 20), Engram on layers 1 and 14 (98 GB FP8 tables each, rows gathered by mmap), vocabulary 129,280. Full model, not a reduced vehicle; MTP (DSpark) not used. Layer-streamed: one layer (7.4 GB) resident at a time.

deployment_arithmetic_sources.contract: tools/hdc_golden_v41.py (last change e4838488) under HDC_V41_ARITH=chunk8 and HDC_V41_FUSE=osm: R-ARITH (docs/ARCH_SPEC_V41.md section 4: every accumulation in contiguous chunks of <= 8 summed sequentially from +0, chunk sums by a pairwise tree padded with +0; FP8/FP4 linears and the index dots as exact 32-element block dots rounded once, blocks by the same chunk-8 tree) plus R-ARITH v2 lever 1, online softmax in the release kernel's 64-entry blocks (decode-kernel row order: window ring oldest first, then the selected compressed rows). Norm folding (nfold) is REJECTED (docs/ARCH_SPEC_V41.md section 12, user decision 2026-09-27) and is not applied.
deployment_arithmetic_sources.special_functions: exp = Cody-Waite + degree-6 Horner (tools/hdc_golden.py 45762e32); rsqrt = bit seed + 3 Newton steps; softplus = max(x,0) + log1p(exp(-|x|)) with log1p by the degree-17 atanh series; sigmoid/SiLU by IEEE division; IEEE sqrt and division; every zero canonical +0; top-k ties to the lower index (router, indexer, candidate blocks).
deployment_arithmetic_sources.fast_adds: The 3-cycle adder (rtl/hdc/ot_hdc_fastfp.sv) is bit-identical to the qualified 5-stage IEEE RNE pipes (its header; rtl/test/tb_hdc_fastfp_equiv.sv): latency only, no numerical effect, so nothing to emulate.
deployment_arithmetic_sources.kv_formats_mode_c: Mode (c) 'deployment + compressed/FP8 KV' IS mode (b): the deployed KV formats are the checkpoint's own -- window KV FP8 E4M3 / UE8M0 per 32 (after kv_norm and RoPE), compressed KV FP4 E2M1 / E4M3 per 16, index keys FP4 E2M1 / UE8M0 per 32 (docs/ARCH_SPEC_V41.md section 5: 'Index keys stay in their model precision ... lossless') -- which both the reference and the golden already apply, and every dequantised value is exactly representable in BF16 (asserted in the run and in the test), so storing codes + scales in HBM and dequantising on read is value-identical to the golden's BF16 quantise-dequantise.

contract_emulation_fidelity: Exact, not approximated. The GPU contract engine (Triton block-dot kernel: exact 32-element FP8xFP8 / FP8xFP4 dots by an error-free split of each exact product into a multiple of 4 and a remainder, one rounding, scaled, chunk-8 over blocks; Triton chunk-8 + pairwise-tree kernel with explicit mul.rn for FP32-weight products; eager IEEE FP32 elementwise golden primitives) reproduces hdc_golden_v41 (chunk8 + osm) bit-exactly in every logit of every position of a 40-token sequence of the reduced vehicle (tests/test_deepseek_v41_deployment_quality.py), and each kernel/primitive/quantiser is bit-exact against the numpy golden over the full E4M3/E2M1 ranges. At the full shape the engine uses the checkpoint's per-32-block Engram row scales (the release's ParallelEngramEmbedding); see golden_issue_found.
reference_fidelity: Mode a runs the release's own inference/model.py modules (Block, Attention with its Compressor/Indexer/candidate blocks, Engram, hyper-connections, RMSNorm, RoPE, Gate, MoE, Expert) layer by layer as the vendor evaluates a prompt (one prefill call per sequence, start_pos 0), with the release's BF16/FP32 TileLang kernels sparse_attn (called on groups of 16 heads: the released 64-head call needs 141,312 B of shared memory, over sm_120's limit; heads are independent in the kernel) and hc_split_sinkhorn. The four FP8/FP4 TileLang kernels are broken on this sm_120 GPU with tilelang 0.1.8 and are replaced by PyTorch restatements of their own formulas: fp4_gemm (NaN at the released expert shape; also recorded by tools/run_deepseek_v41_reduced_reference_oracle.py) and fp8_gemm (NaN at wo_b, K = 8,192, and at wq_a inside a real prefill) by the same codes and block scales dequantised exactly and one cuBLAS FP32 GEMM (BF16 out); act_quant / fp4_act_quant (emit NaN E4M3 codes: 1,426 of 2.6M codes of layer 0's attention input on WikiText) by the same scale rule, clamp, round-to-nearest-even and dequantisation. The released kernels also touch rows past a tensor whose row count is not a multiple of 32 (run-dependent MoE output, measured); all row-tiled replacements are row-exact. Mode a therefore = vendor model code + vendor attention/Sinkhorn kernels + exact dequantised GEMMs with FP32 accumulation.
noise_floor_mode_a2: Mode a2 is this tool's own implementation of the release semantics (same quantisation and BF16 storage points as the golden) on standard GPU arithmetic: cuBLAS FP32 GEMMs of the dequantised operands, torch exp/rsqrt/softplus/sigmoid/SiLU, a plain two-pass softmax over the whole selected row set, torch.topk. a vs a2 is the spread between two legitimate GPU implementations of the same checkpoint -- the scale against which the contract's b vs a is read.
teacher_forced_modes: b_tf / a2_tf run layer L on the reference's own input to layer L (their own compressed-KV/index-key/selection chain), so their router/index flip rates and hidden divergences are those of one layer's arithmetic; b / a2 are free-running (accumulated). Teacher-forced modes run on the first 8 WikiText windows (16,384 positions).

evaluation_protocol.wikitext2: Salesforce/wikitext wikitext-2-raw-v1 test, '\n\n'.join, DeepSeek-V4.1 tokenizer; 16 non-overlapping windows of 2,048 tokens (BOS + 2,047 text tokens) evenly spaced over the split, every position after BOS scored (32,752 predictions); PPL = exp(mean NLL). CIs: paired bootstrap over windows (2,000 resamples).
evaluation_protocol.mmlu: cais/mmlu all/test, 200 questions sampled with numpy seed 0 (sorted), zero-shot 'Answer:' prompt with BOS, argmax over the ' A'..' D' logits at the last prompt position (sequences right-padded into batches; causal, so padding never reaches a scored position); CI bootstrap over questions, delta paired.
evaluation_protocol.selection_flips: router: fraction of (real) positions whose top-6 expert SET differs from mode a's at that layer; index: fraction of queries whose selected compressed-position set differs, and the fraction of selected positions changed, at the eight index-source layers.

golden_issue_found: tools/hdc_golden_v41.py:706 keeps only column 0 of layers.{L}.engram.embed.scale (self.emb_codes ... [:, 0]) and :796 scales a whole Engram row by it. The reduced vehicle has one 32-block per row (head_dim 32) so it is exact there, but the released table has head_dim 256 = 8 UE8M0 block scales per row, and 87% of sampled rows (2,000 random rows of layer 1) carry different scales across their blocks: at the shipped shape the golden would mis-scale 7/8 of each Engram row (the release's ParallelEngramEmbedding applies a scale per 32-block). Not edited here (Codex owns golden edits); this tool applies per-block scales, identical to the golden wherever the golden is right.
approximations_and_not_run: Mode a is not the unmodified release kernel stack: its FP8/FP4 GEMMs and activation quantisers are exact PyTorch restatements (the TileLang kernels produce NaN on this GPU); its FP8 GEMMs therefore accumulate in FP32 (cuBLAS) instead of the tensor-core FP8 MMA.

Evaluation size: 16 WikiText-2 windows at 2K (32,752 scored tokens) and 200 MMLU questions, sized to one ~3-hour pass of the full model on a shared GPU; no 4K+ context, no C4, no GSM8K, no free-running greedy generation (layer streaming processes every sequence through layer L before L+1, so autoregressive decoding is not possible in this design).
Teacher-forced (per-layer, one-layer) flip rates use 8 of the 16 windows.

Prefill evaluation: every position is teacher-forced over the true text; the contract's per-position arithmetic is the golden's decode step (the golden's forward_positions is position-exact), so this is the arithmetic a deployed decode would apply to the same prefix.
MTP/DSpark heads not evaluated (not needed for next-token quality).
8-bit activations: the checkpoint's own FP8 activation quantisation is applied in every mode; no further activation format exists in the V4.1 contract.

conclusion.verdict: ACCEPTABLE under the pre-registered rule. The deployment contract (b) changes WikiText-2 perplexity by +0.09% [-0.38%, +0.58%] (2.6166 vs 2.6142, 16 x 2K windows) and MMLU by +1.0 pt [0.0, +2.5] (88.0% vs 87.0%, 200 questions, 98.5% same answers). Both are indistinguishable from the spread between two legitimate GPU arithmetics: a2 vs a gives -0.12% [-0.48%, +0.24%] PPL and -0.5 pt [-2.5, +1.5] MMLU.
conclusion.agreement: Top-1 agreement with the reference: b 95.64%, a2 95.61%; mean KL(a||.) 0.0235 vs 0.0241 nats. Disagreements sit at near-ties (median reference top-1 margin 0.27 logits; 91% below 1 logit).
conclusion.expert_selection_flips: One layer's arithmetic (teacher-forced, b_tf) flips the top-6 expert set of 0.70% of tokens per layer on average (max 1.14%, layer 1) and changes 0.05% of selected index positions (max 0.09%, layer 24); a second GPU implementation (a2_tf) flips 1.03% / 0.04%. Free-running, flips accumulate through depth to 30% of tokens per layer on average (45% at layer 38) with 4.4% of index selections changed -- identically for b (30.0%) and a2 (30.2%) -- while quality does not move: routing among near-equal experts is sensitive to ulp-level noise but the choice does not affect next-token quality. The atlas' reduced-vehicle observation (summation order flips expert selection) holds on the full model and is harmless there.
conclusion.summary: Every measured effect of the contract is at or below the noise floor of reordering FP32 sums on a GPU (a vs a2), and far inside the thresholds (2% PPL, 1 pt MMLU).

resources: Wall 6,866 s for 40 layers (one checkpoint pass). Host: anonymous RSS <= 6.5 GB (peak total RSS 38.8 GB of which the rest is reclaimable file-backed mmap page cache), under systemd-run MemoryMax=16G; GPU peak 23.8 GB.

threshold.rule: the deployment contract (b) is acceptable iff, against the vendor reference (a), WikiText-2 perplexity rises by at most 2.0% (relative) AND MMLU accuracy falls by at most 1.0 point (point estimates; paired 95% bootstrap CIs reported beside them). Top-1 agreement, KL, and the per-layer router/index selection flip rates are reported against the a-vs-a2 noise floor of two legitimate GPU arithmetics; they are descriptive, not gating. Fixed before any full-model result was seen.
